title: UNIT ONE: INTRODUCTION TO HISTORY AND HISTORIOGRAPHY
content:
ሰላም የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! 👋 እንኳን ወደ History of Ethiopia and the Horn (Hist. 1012) Unit 1 ትምህርት በሰላም መጣችሁ! ይህ ማስታወሻ ሞጁሉን መስመር በመስመር ተከትሎ፣ ለፈተና 100% ሙሉ በሙሉ እንድትዘጋጁ ተደርጎ በጥራት የተዘጋጀ የEthioFresh Tutorial ነው። ትኩረታችሁን ሰብሰብ አድርጉ... ታሪክን በደስታ እንማራለን! 🚀

1.1. Nature and Uses of History

1.1.1. Nature of History
• Etymology: The word history originates from the Greek word istoria, which means "learning through enquiry" or "an account of one's inquiries."
• Father of History: The Greek historian Herodotus (c. 484–425 BC) was the first writer to systematically investigate and document historical events, earning him the title "father of history."
• Ordinary Usage vs. Academic Definition:
- Ordinary Usage: History refers to all things that have occurred in the human past.
- Academic Definition: History is the systematic study and organized knowledge of the past, involving the discovery, collection, organization, and presentation of information about past events.
• Distinction: There is a clear difference between what actually happened in the past (which exists independently and awaits recording) and the accounts of the past reconstructed by historians.
• Purpose: History aims not merely to produce a chronology of events, but to identify patterns and establish meaning through rigorous study and interpretation of sources.
• Difference from Other Disciplines: While other social sciences study the interaction between humans and their environment in the present, history studies this interaction in the past within the framework of continuous change over time.
• Periodization: Historians organize and divide the past into distinct periods based on significant developments (conventionally divided into ancient, medieval, and modern).
• Continuity and Change: Continuities or persisting patterns exist over long periods (such as basic societal fabrics), but this does not mean nothing changes. Human life changes continuously across social, cultural, economic, and political aspects.

👉 History የሚለው ቃል የመጣው istoria ከሚለው የጽርዕ (ግሪክ) ቃል ሲሆን ትርጉሙም "በምርምር ወይም በጥያቄ መረዳት/ማወቅ" ማለት ነው። ሄሮዶተስ (Herodotus) የመጀመሪያው ታሪካዊ ክስተቶችን በስርዓት መዝግቦ ያስቀመጠ በመሆኑ "የታሪክ አባት" ይባላል። ታሪክ ማለት ዝም ብሎ የነገሮች ቅደም ተከተል (chronology) ብቻ ሳይሆን፣ ያለፉ ድርጊቶችን በመመርመር ትርጉም እና ስርዓት ማውጣት ነው። ታሪክ ከሌሎች የማህበራዊ ሳይንስ ትምህርቶች የሚለየው የሰው ልጅንና የአካባቢውን ግንኙነት በአለፈው ጊዜ (in the past) እና በጊዜ ሂደት ውስጥ በሚመጣ ለወጥ (change over time) ላይ አተኩሮ ስለሚያጠና ነው። ታሪክ አላስፈላጊ ውታፍ እያዩ እንዳይደናገሩ ጊዜን በዘመን ይከፋፍላል፤ ይህም Periodization (Ancient, Medieval, Modern) ይባላል።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Key Exam Distinction: Other social sciences study human-environment interaction in the PRESENT; History studies it in the PAST within a time continuum.
• Istoria Definition: Always remember the exact phrase "learning through enquiry".

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: 'History is just studying old gossip with dates!' ይላሉ አንዳንዶች... ነገር ግን በፈተና ላይ A+ የሚያስገኝልህ ዋናው ሚስጥር የኢስቶሪያ (Istoria) ትርጉም ነው! 😜


1.1.2. Uses of History
Why do we study the past when we live in the present and plan for the future?

1. History Helps Us Understand the Present:
It serves as a storehouse of information analyzing how people behaved and acted in the past. Present problems cannot be fully understood without tracing their historical origins.

2. History Provides a Sense of Identity:
Knowledge of history is indispensable for understanding who we are. Analogy: As memory is to the individual, history is to society. A society without history cannot define its identity or make intelligent decisions.

3. History Helps Develop Tolerance and Open-Mindedness:
By studying different cultures and societies of the past, students are freed from inherent cultural provincialism (ethnocentrism) and acquire broad-mindedness and flexibility.

4. History Teaches Critical Skills:
It helps develop research skills, source evaluation, coherent argument construction based on evidence, and analytical/communication skills essential for day-to-day decision-making.

5. History Provides a Basic Background for Other Disciplines:
It is valuable for literature, art, philosophy, religion, sociology, political science, anthropology, and economics. History is considered the "mother discipline" because these subjects arose out of historical investigation.

6. History Provides Endless Source of Fascination:
Exploring past human lives offers wonder, excitement, and aesthetic appreciation.

Abuse of History:
History can be abused through deliberate manipulation to fit current political agendas ("history written backwards" to justify the present). Historians must avoid propaganda by subjecting ideas to independent external verification.

👉 ታሪክን የምናጠናው ለምንድነው?
1. ያሁኑን ለማወቅ: የዛሬ ችግሮቻችንን ስራቸውን ለማወቅ ያግዛል።
2. ማንነትን ለማወቅ: "አእምሮ/ትውስታ ለግለሰብ እንደሆነው ሁሉ፣ ታሪክም ለማህበረሰብ ነው!" ታሪክ የሌለው ማህበረሰብ ማንነቱን አያውቅም።
3. ትዕግስትና ሰፊ አስተሳሰብ ለማዳበር: የሌሎችን ባህል በመረዳት ጠባብነትን (provincialism) ያስወግዳል።
4. የምርምርና የመተንተን ክህሎት ለማሳደግ: መረጃን የመመዘን እና የማስረዳት አቅምን ይገነባል።
5. ለሌሎች ትምህርቶች መሰረት በመሆኑ: ታሪክ የሌሎች ትምህርቶች "Mother Discipline" (የእናት ትምህርት) ይባላል።
6. ደስታና ጉጉት ስለሚፈጥር።
⚠️ የታሪክ አላግባብ መጠቀም (Abuse of History): ታሪክን ለፖለቲካ ጥቅም ሲባል ማዛባት እና ወደ ኋላ መገልበጥ ("history written backwards") የታሪክ አላግባብ መጠቀም ይባላል።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Analogy Question: "Memory is to individual as _____ is to society." ⇒ Answer: History.
• Term Question: History is known as the Mother Discipline.


1.2. Sources and Methods of Historical Study
Historians are not creative writers (like novelists); their work must be supported by evidence derived from historical sources.

Classification of Historical Sources:

1. Primary Sources:
• Surviving traces of the past available in the present that are original or first-hand in proximity to the event in time and space.
• Examples: Manuscripts (handwritten materials), diaries, letters, minutes, inscriptions, chronicles, hagiographies, court records, administrative files, travel documents, photos, maps, audiovisual materials, coins, fossils, weapons, utensils, and buildings.

2. Secondary Sources:
• Second-hand accounts of past events written after the event occurred, providing an interpretation based on primary sources.
• Examples: Articles, books, textbooks, biographies, theses, dissertations, reports, and historical movies/stories.

3. Oral Data:
• Essential for studying non-literate societies.
• Oral Tradition: Information transmitted from generation to generation via folk songs, folk sayings, etc.
• Oral History: Oral testimonies of lived experiences by eye-witnesses (functions as a primary source).

Critical Evaluation of Sources:
• Primary sources must be verified for originality and authenticity (to detect forgeries).
• Secondary sources must be examined for reliability of reconstruction.
• Oral data must be cross-checked to avoid distortion over time.

👉 የታሪክ ተመራማሪዎች እንደ ልቦለድ ፀሐፊዎች ከጭንቅላታቸው አይጽፉም፤ መረጃ (sources) ያስፈልጋቸዋል። የታሪክ መረጃዎች በሶስት ይከፈላሉ፡
1. የመጀመሪያ ደረጃ መረጃዎች (Primary Sources): ድርጊቱ በተፈፀመበት ጊዜና ቦታ የነበሩ ቀጥተኛ መረጃዎች ናቸው (ምሳሌ፡ የእጅ ጽሁፎች፣ ማስታወሻዎች፣ ሳንቲሞች፣ ህንፃዎች፣ ቅሪተ አካላት፣ ዜና መዋዕሎች)።
2. ሁለተኛ ደረጃ መረጃዎች (Secondary Sources): ድርጊቱ ከተፈፀመ በኋላ የመረጃ ምንጮችን በማጣቀስ የተጻፉ ናቸው (ምሳሌ፡ መጻህፍት፣ መጣጥፎች፣ የመመረቂያ ጽሁፎች)።
3. የቃል መረጃ (Oral Data): የቃል ታሪክ (Oral History - በዓይን የታየ የመጀመሪያ ደረጃ) እና የቃል መረጃ (Oral Tradition - የትውልድ ቅብብል) በመባል ይከፈላሉ።
⚠️ መረጃዎችን መፈተሽ: የመጀመሪያ ደረጃ መረጃዎች ትክክለኛነት (authenticity) መረጋገጥ አለበት (ምክንያቱም ሀሰተኛ ሊሆኑ ስለሚችሉ)።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Exam Trick: Is Oral History primary or secondary? If it is a direct eye-witness account of a lived experience, it serves as a PRIMARY source!


1.3. Historiography of Ethiopia and the Horn
Historiography is the history of historical writing. It studies how knowledge of the past is obtained, transmitted, and changed over time.

Global Historiography Origins:
• Ancient Greece: Herodotus and Thucydides (c. 455–400 BC).
• China: Sima Qian (145–86 BC).
• 19th Century Europe: History became an academic discipline. Leopold Von Ranke (1795–1886) established research methods in Berlin and is considered the "father of modern historiography."

Development of Historiography in Ethiopia and the Horn:

1. Earliest External Sources:
• Periplus of the Erythrean Sea: Written in the 1st century AD by an anonymous author.
• Christian Topography: Written in the 6th century AD by Cosmas Indicopleustes (a Greek sailor).

2. Early Indigenous Manuscripts and Hagiographies:
• Earliest Ethiopian manuscript: 7th-century AD illustrated manuscript at Abba Gerima monastery (Adwa).
• 13th-century manuscript at Haiq Estifanos monastery (Wollo).
• Hagiographies (Gadl): Christian biographies of saints (contain marginalia notes). Muslim hagiographical tradition: Life of Shaykh Ja’far Bukko of Gattira (Wollo, late 19th C).

3. Royal Chronicles (ዜና መዋዕል):
• Written by court scribes or clergymen.
• Earliest Chronicle: The Glorious Victories of Amde-Tsion (14th century).
• Last Chronicle: Chronicle of Abeto Iyasu and Empress Zewditu (20th century).

4. Arabic Accounts and Foreign Travelers:
• Arabic Accounts: al-Masudi (10th C) and Ibn Battuta (14th C).
• Futuh al-Habasha (The Conquest of Abyssinia): Written in the 16th century by Shihab al-Din (documents Christian-Adal wars).
• Al-Haymi: Documented the 1647 Yemeni delegation to King Fasiledas.
• Abba Bahrey: Ge'ez account of Oromo socio-political organization written in 1593.
• European Travelers: Francisco Alvarez (The Prester John of the Indies, 16th C), James Bruce (Travels to Discover the Source of the Nile, 18th C).
• Hiob Ludolf (1624–1704): Wrote Historia Aethiopica with information from Abba Gorgorios (Abba Gregory). Ludolf is considered the "founder of Ethiopian studies as an academic discipline in Europe."

5. Early 20th Century Ethiopian Intellectuals:
• Shifted away from adulatory chronicle writing toward critical social, administrative, and economic analysis.
• Pioneers: Aleqa Taye Gebre-Mariam, Aleqa Atsme Giorgis Gebre Mesih, Debtera Fisseha-Giorgis Abyezgi, Negadrases Afework Gebre-Iyesus, Gebre-Hiwot Baykedagn, Blatten Geta Hiruy Wolde-Selassie.

6. Post-Liberation Period:
• Tekle-Tsadik Mekuria: Bridge between pre-1935 writers and modern professional historians.
• Yilma Deressa: Wrote YeItyopiya Tarik Be’asra Sidistegnaw Kifle Zemen.
• Blatten Geta Mahteme-Selassie Wolde-Meskel: Wrote Zikre Neger (administrative system, land tenure, taxation).
• Dejjazmach Kebede Tesema: Wrote Yetarik Mastawesha (1962 E.C.).

7. Professionalization of History (1960s):
• 1963: Department of History opened at Haile Selassie I University (HSIU).
• 1963: Institute of Ethiopian Studies (IES) founded.
• Richard Pankhurst: First Director of IES, prolific writer, published Journal of Ethiopian Studies.

👉 ሂስቶሪዮግራፊ (Historiography) ማለት " የታሪክ አጻጻፍ ታሪክ" ማለት ነው።
• ሊዮፖልድ ቮን ራንኬ (Leopold Von Ranke): የዘመናዊ ሂስቶሪዮግራፊ አባት ይባላል።
• የመጀመሪያዎቹ የውጭ የጽሁፍ መረጃዎች: Periplus of the Erythrean Sea (1ኛ ክፍለ ዘመን) እና Christian Topography በኮስማስ (6ኛ ክፍለ ዘመን)።
• የመጀመሪያው የሀገር ውስጥ ጽሁፍ: የአባ ገሪማ ገዳም በእጅ የተጻፈ ወንጌል (7ኛ ክፍለ ዘመን)።
• የመጀመሪያው ዜና መዋዕል (Chronicle): የዐምደ ጽዮን ዜና መዋዕል (14ኛ ክፍለ ዘመን)።
• የመጨረሻው ዜና መዋዕል: የኢያሱ እና የዘውዲቱ ዜና መዋዕል (20ኛ ክፍለ ዘመን)።
• ፉቱህ አል ሀበሻ (Futuh al-Habasha): በሺሃብ አድ-ዲን (Shihab al-Din) የተጻፈ የ16ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን የክርስቲያንና አዳል ሱልጣኔት ጦርነት ታሪክ።
• ሂዮብ ሉዶልፍ (Hiob Ludolf): ከአባ ጎርጎርዮስ ጋር በመሆን Historia Aethiopicaን የጻፈ ሲሆን፣ በአውሮፓ "የኢትዮጵያ ጥናት መስራች" (Founder of Ethiopian Studies in Europe) ይባላል።
• 1960ዎቹ: በ1955 ዓ.ም (1963 G.C) የኢትዮጵያ ጥናትና ምርምር ተቋም (IES) እና የታሪክ ትምህርት ክፍል በኃይለስላሴ 1ኛ ዩኒቨርሲቲ ተከፈተ። ሪቻርድ ፓንክኸርስት የመጀመሪያው የ IES ዳይሬክተር ነበሩ።

💡 Exam Hints (ከፍተኛ ትኩረት የሚሹ):
• Father of Modern Historiography ⇒ Leopold Von Ranke.
• Founder of Ethiopian Studies in Europe ⇒ Hiob Ludolf (with Abba Gorgorios).
• Author of Futuh al-Habasha ⇒ Shihab al-Din.
• Earliest Chronicle ⇒ The Glorious Victories of Amde-Tsion.
• First Director of IES ⇒ Richard Pankhurst.


1.4. Geographical Context
"Ethiopia and the Horn" refers to Northeast Africa comprising Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia.

Topography and Environmental Zones:
1. Eastern Lowlands: Coastal strip of NE Eritrea, Danakil Depression, lower Awash, Ogaden, Somalia. Hot and dry climate.
2. Highland Massif: From northern Eritrea to southern Ethiopia, divided into Western and Eastern highlands by the Rift Valley.
3. Western Lowlands: Foothills bordering Sudan with hot climate and thick forests along river banks.

Five Principal Drainage Systems:
Drainage SystemKey Characteristics & Flow
1. Nile SystemBlue Nile (Abay - starts at Lake Tana) + White Nile meet in Khartoum ⇒ flows to Egypt & Mediterranean Sea.
2. Awash SystemEntirely Ethiopian system! Links central highlands to hot lowlands of Danakil Depression.
3. Rift Valley Lakes SystemSelf-contained basin stretching from Lake Ziway to Lake Turkana (formerly Rudolf).
4. Gibe–Gojeb–Omo SystemLinks SW Ethiopia to semi-desert lowlands of northern Kenya (Lake Turkana).
5. Shebele & Genale SystemOriginate in Eastern highlands. Genale (Jubba) reaches Indian Ocean; Shebele disappears in the sand before reaching the ocean.


👉 የኢትዮጵያ እና የአፍሪካ ቀንድ ሀገራት የሚባሉት፡ ኢትዮጵያ፣ ኤርትራ፣ ጅቡቲ እና ሶማሊያ ናቸው።
አምስቱ ዋና ዋና የወንዝ ተፋሰሶች:
1. የአባይ (ናይል) ተፋሰስ: ጣና ሀይቅ ተነስቶ ከነጭ ናይል ጋር ካርቱም ላይ ይቀላቀላል።
2. የአዋሽ ተፋሰስ: ሙሉ በሙሉ በኢትዮጵያ ውስጥ ብቻ የሚፈስ ወንዝ ነው! ከማዕከላዊ ደጋማ ቦታዎች ተነስቶ ዳናኪል በረሃ ይገባል።
3. የስምጥሸለቆ ሀይቆች ተፋሰስ: ከዝዋይ እስከ ቱርካና (ሩዶልፍ) ሀይቅ ይዘረጋል።
4. የጊቤ-ጎጀብ-ኦሞ ተፋሰስ: ወደ ቱርካና ሀይቅ ይፈሳል።
5. የሸበሌ እና ገናሌ ተፋሰስ: ገናሌ (ጁባ) ህንድ ውቅያኖስ ሲደርስ፣ ሸበሌ ግን ሶማሊያ አሸዋ ውስጥ ይሰምጣል!

💡 Exam Hints:
• Which river system is ENTIRELY contained within Ethiopia? ⇒ Awash River System.
• Which river disappears in the sand near the coastline? ⇒ Shebele River.
• Which river reaches the Indian Ocean? ⇒ Genale (Jubba) River.
